Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

rePredRet (development version)

Prediction intervals

  • New default interval method method = "adaptive_pi" (gam_adaptive_pi()) in build_model(), build_all_models(), build_all_models_furrr() and build_user_models(). The interval width follows the local scatter of the calibration compounds (a Gamma GAM of cross-validated absolute residuals, weighted to ignore outliers) and is calibrated by cross-validated conformal prediction. On held-out compounds from 135 RepoRT system pairs it covered 94.6% (95% nominal), equally in low- and high-scatter regions (94.8% / 94.5%). It takes 60-90 ms per model.
  • method = "fast_ci" (gam_fast_ci()) is kept as the fast option (15-20 ms per model), with fixes: the residual variance comes from leave-one-out residuals instead of in-sample residuals (coverage 93.9% -> 95.5%; with 10-15 compounds 83% -> 90%), and the bounds are made monotone by isotonic regression instead of a running maximum, which narrowed the lower side. Its width is still nearly constant (97.4% / 93.4% coverage in low- / high-scatter regions).
  • method = "bootstrap" was a confidence interval of the curve, not a prediction interval (59% coverage; 53% with 200+ compounds). It now uses the out-of-bag predictions as out-of-sample residuals with the same local scale and conformal calibration as adaptive_pi (94.8% coverage). boot2ci_PI() has a new signature and the unused boot2ci() was removed.
  • With 10-15 compounds no method reaches the nominal coverage (86-90%); this is now documented.
  • All methods truncate the lower bound at 0.
  • Model statistics (model.json stats and model$stats) gain r_squared, coverage (fraction of calibration compounds inside the PI) and rel_mean_ci_width (mean PI width / target RT range).
  • Removed the unused gam_prediction_intervals(), gam_prediction_intervals_parallel(), fit_gam_mono_once() and gam_fast_pi().
  • build_all_models_furrr() and build_all_models() rebuild cached models that were built with another interval method, method version (pi_method_version()) or alpha, so the next pipeline run rebuilds all models.
  • Small source-RT jitter (fewer than 4 distinct RTs) uses a fixed seed, so the same data always give the same model.
  • build_model() returns status "fit_failed" instead of a model with non-finite predictions or intervals.
  • The monotone GAM fit is shared by all interval methods (fit_gam_mono()). Its sigmoid outlier weights (0.1, 30) were set by eye for the original PredRet and have never been optimized; this is now documented.
  • New article “Prediction interval benchmark”, and the benchmark script inst/benchmark/pi_benchmark.R.
  • withr moved from Suggests to Imports; MASS is no longer needed.

Breaking changes

  • Removed rePredRet_download(), rePredRet_predict(), rePredRet_system_predictions() and rePredRet_plot_errors(). They depended on a rePredRet-data repository with pre-computed predictions that does not exist. Use build_user_models() and predict_rt_user() to predict RTs.
  • Removed rePredRet_plot_model(); use plot_model().
  • rePredRet_systems(), rePredRet_models(), rePredRet_model(), plot_model() and rePredRet_plot_network() now fetch files on demand from the rePredRet-models repository and cache them locally. Their data_path argument is replaced by refresh. rePredRet_model() returns the contents of model.json.
  • Requires R >= 4.4.0.

Bug fixes

  • save_model_plot() (and build_all_models(save_plots = TRUE)) failed because the internal plot function was masked by the exported plot_model().
  • plot_model() read model statistics from the wrong index columns.
  • search_compound() and get_system_info() looked for RepoRT data in the wrong directory when downloading it.
  • Model viewer: loads the index from the right location, parses it correctly, plots the model data and draws the interval band between the bounds. It is now part of the website.
  • build_user_models(), build_model() and build_all_models() default to parallelly::availableCores().

Website

  • The Overview, Model Statistics and Network articles are computed from the published model index when the site is built, instead of from statistics files committed in January (a 642-model test run). The site is rebuilt after each model update.
  • Removed the Predictions article and the committed prediction and statistics files; pre-computed predictions are no longer produced.
  • Removed the old standalone Quarto site in website/; the pkgdown site replaces it.

Other

  • rePredRet_plot_network() gains show_labels.
  • inst/scripts/run_pipeline.R writes to output/ by default (was website/data/).
  • Runner setup (github_runner.yml, RUNNER_SETUP.md): host paths are set in .env and must be on local disks; adds the /opt/repredret-cache mount.

Pipeline

  • build_all_models_furrr() now builds incrementally: only models whose datasets changed or whose files are missing are rebuilt. Previously the build cache was loaded but never applied or saved, so every run rebuilt all models.
  • build_all_models_furrr() removes models for removed datasets and pairs that no longer have enough common compounds, keeps model_index.csv complete across incremental runs, records report_version in the build cache and returns changed.
  • Model pairs are found with a sparse overlap matrix and RT matrices come from a per-dataset lookup, instead of calling get_common_compounds() for every ordered pair (minutes to seconds on the full RepoRT data).
  • The number of workers defaults to parallelly::availableCores(), which respects container CPU limits (parallel::detectCores() reports all host cores).
  • A failing model no longer aborts the whole build.
  • CI: tracks RepoRT master commits instead of releases and only pushes to the data repository when models changed. max_systems test runs no longer touch the published models.
  • CI: models are built directly in a persistent clone of rePredRet-models on the runner (/opt/repredret-cache), which is reset to the published state at the start of each run. Only changed model directories are committed and pushed, in chunks, instead of force-pushing a freshly created repository with all models.

rePredRet 0.2.0

New Features

User Model Building

  • build_user_models(): Build calibration models from your own RT data to all compatible RepoRT systems
  • predict_rt_user(): Generate RT predictions using user-built models
  • UserRTModels S4 class: Stores models with diagnostics, supports show(), summary(), plot(), [[]] methods
  • UserRTPredictions S4 class: Stores predictions, supports show(), summary(), as.data.frame(), plot() methods

Utility Functions

  • plot_model(): Plot pre-built models from the data repository with ggplot2/plotly
  • search_compound(): Search for compounds by InChI across all systems
  • search_compounds(): Batch search for multiple InChIs
  • compare_systems(): Rank repository systems by similarity to user’s data
  • get_system_info(): Get detailed system metadata (column, gradient, etc.)
  • export_predictions(): Export predictions to CSV or Excel format
  • validate_models(): Cross-validation for assessing model quality
  • check_input_data(): Validate InChIs and RTs before model building

Visualizations

  • plot_system_network(): Visualize system connectivity
  • plot_prediction_errors(): Error distribution plots
  • plot_compound_coverage(): Heatmap of compound presence across systems

Improvements

  • All InChI matching now consistently strips stereochemistry layers (/t, /b, /m, /s)
  • predict_rt_user() returns only the best prediction per compound (narrowest CI)
  • Added progress bars for long-running operations
  • Added comprehensive unit tests
  • Added pkgdown documentation website
  • Added GitHub Actions for R CMD check and code coverage

Documentation

  • New tutorial: “Predict RT for Your Own Data”
  • New function reference page
  • Vignette for offline documentation

rePredRet 0.1.0

  • Initial release
  • Core model building functions: build_model(), build_all_models(), build_all_models_furrr()
  • Prediction functions: predict_rt(), generate_all_predictions()
  • Data loading: download_report(), load_report_data(), get_common_compounds()
  • User query functions: rePredRet_download(), rePredRet_predict(), rePredRet_systems(), rePredRet_models()
  • GAM fitting with monotonic constraints and confidence intervals
  • Fast CI calculation method (72x faster than bootstrap)
